messages:
alex: FYI customer ACME-facing endpoint hitting p99 ~2.3s since 09:40 UTC, p50 unchanged. customer says tail feels intermittent. tagging oncall.
jamie: sending traces and logs now, seeing a clump of tiny requests that wait for batch fill then blow past SLOs. looks like continuous-batcher hold-window hitting max_wait on many tiny prompts.
alex: can you paste the trace id?
jamie: trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d, logs show microbatch.size=1 but microbatch.wait_ms ~120ms before dispatch, then GPU queuing + kv-merge adds ~1.8s.
maria: hmm that matches the dashboard — coalescer_requests count spikes during the incident, batcher.inflight shows many tiny batches that wait for size threshold 8 for short-lived traffic.
ryan: customer traffic pattern: many single-token chat pings (heartbeat-style), so continuous batcher is deliberately waiting for size to reduce token cost but harming tail latency.
alex: ops-bot, flagging customer-impacting p99.
ops-bot: incident created #INC-7891, paging oncall.
jamie: repro locally with loadgen: 500 rps, payloads size 6 tokens, interarrival jitter 0-20ms. command: 
```
loadgen --rps 500 --payloads small_prompts.json --jitter 20 --duration 300
```
results: p50=80ms, p95=190ms, p99=2.1s. toggling batcher.max_wait_ms to 15ms -> p99 drops to 220ms.
alex: good repro. can we do a short-term config change for this customer? maybe per-tenant override: if avg_tokens < 10 -> max_wait_ms=15 and bypass size threshold?
maria: we already support routing by tenant policy, but need a safe rollout. quick mitigation: enable "eager_send_for_small_prompts" (experimental) per route, which sends partial batches when avg_tokens < threshold. I can flip for ACME and monitor.
ryan: note tradeoff: cost will go up ~12-18% due to less batching, but customer SLA > p99 500ms is more important.
jamie: propose hotpatch script for console API: 
```
# set route override
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/routes/ACME/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"batching": {"eager_send_for_small_prompts": true, "max_wait_ms": 15}}'
```
I'll run in canary on 2 hosts then roll.
alex: please also add a short circuit so if cpu/gpu busy >75% we revert to original behavior (avoid thrash).
maria: ack, adding revert condition to the rollout script.
ops-bot: alert: rollout started 09:58 UTC.
jamie: after canary p99 down to 210-260ms for ACME, logs show much fewer max_wait expirations.
ryan: verify metrics for cost impact and token throughput.
alex: customer update prepared: "we identified continuous-batcher heuristics that delayed very small prompts; temporary per-route override applied to prioritize latency — we expect p99 improvement within minutes; cost delta monitored."
maria: rolling to remaining hosts now. will keep the revert trigger (gpu_util>75%) in place.
jamie: adding repro notes to ticket: steps, loadgen command, trace id, and the console override snippet.
ryan: long-term: we should add an adaptive batcher mode: detect micropayload traffic and shift to time-first strategy. file a story?
alex: please create an eng-ticket and link to console feature flag + dashboard alert. prioritize after current oncall work.
maria: created ENG-2146: "adaptive_batcher: time-first mode for micropayloads" with acceptance criteria and perf regressions matrix.
ops-bot: incident INC-7891 resolved 10:12 UTC — p99 within SLO, customer acknowledged. :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks team. leave the per-route override for 24h then assess rollback.
jamie: will follow up with a short postmortem and recommended defaults for continuous-batcher config.
ryan: also adding a dashboard tile for micropayload fraction and a threshold alert.
alex: nice work — move to postmortem and docs update. :thumbsup:
